theme: dati personali, famiglia, descrivere le persone
grammar: essere / avere, articles, noun and adjective agreement.

words.ex: Qual è il Suo codice fiscale?

words.en: to grow up; irregular, takes essere (cresciuto)
to know (a person), to meet; avere (conosciuto)
to get along with; irregular (vado), essere
Where are you from? (formal; informal: Di dove sei?)

sentences.it: Mio padre ha ottant'anni, porta gli occhiali e ha i baffi bianchi.
sentences.en: My father is eighty, wears glasses and has a white moustache.
sentences.note: age uses avere; "bianchi" is masc. plural to match "baffi" (bianco -> bianchi, adding h).

sentences.it: Mio cognato è un uomo serio e un po' testardo, ma ha un buon carattere.
sentences.en: My brother-in-law is a serious and somewhat stubborn man, but he has a good personality.
sentences.note: "buono" shortens to "buon" before a masculine singular noun, like "un".

sentences.it: Le mie cognate sono allegre e hanno i capelli ricci.
sentences.en: My sisters-in-law are cheerful and have curly hair.
sentences.note: fem. plural: "le mie ... allegre"; riccio -> ricci (one i, not two).

sentences.it: Ho il codice fiscale, ma non ho ancora la carta d'identità italiana.
sentences.en: I have my tax code, but I don't have an Italian ID card yet.
sentences.note: Italian keeps the article where English uses "my" or nothing (il codice, la carta); "non ... ancora" = not yet.

sentences.it: Mia sorella va d'accordo con il suo fidanzato, ma lui sembra un po' pigro.
sentences.en: My sister gets along with her boyfriend, but he seems a bit lazy.
sentences.note: "mia sorella" has no article (close family, singular), but "il suo fidanzato" does: fidanzato isn't in that family group.

schema:
Adjectives match the noun in gender and number. Adjectives ending in -o have four forms; those ending in -e have two. Watch spelling: -co/-ca usually adds h in the plural, and -io drops one i.
  -o: serio, seria, seri, serie
  -e: felice, felice, felici, felici
  -co: bianco, bianca, bianchi, bianche
  -io: riccio, riccia, ricci, ricce
